scope: Phases 3 and 4 of Append Lanes v2 (asked by maestro.b for a.maestro): presigned URLs, orphaned blobs, crypto, logs, and whether Phase 4 grants can serve as the /send/ endorsement.
basis: the-cyber-boardroom/SGraph-AI__App__Send branch claude/vault-inbox-append-api-jj79bn at c615d0a, the dev plan v0.33.69 (sha256 784bb3b29f00b995...); a.maestro's review at Site__Agent__Maestro dev. Not read: the architect review and the AppSec review (AS-1 to AS-16), known to me only through the plan's 'changes agreed' tables. No code exists yet; this is a design opinion.
verdict: agree with conditions, for both phases

phase_3.reason: Pinning Content-Length, x-amz-checksum-sha256, If-None-Match: * and the tag in the signature (3.4, with a test on the exact signed-header list) is the right control. Conditions: (1) one expiry, 300 s; the body still says 900 s and the risk table 15 minutes, so align the text with 3.3; (2) the object key is built only by the server from sha256(token) and the validated 64-hex blob id (3.1, 3.4), never from client text; (3) a test that a PUT without the checksum header, with another size, or over an existing object, is refused by S3 (LocalStack and once on real S3, as LocalStack may not enforce conditional writes).

Served from the S3 host as application/octet-stream with Content-Disposition attachment (3.5), so a blob can never run as a page on an app origin. Conditions: the server builds each GET only under the caller's own lane prefix, so an enum key cannot reach another lane's blobs by id; 5-minute life; clients treat the URLs as secrets (not logged, not put in pages or messages).

Requiring a retention class when blobs are on is the main fix, and blob_retention_days bounds cost. Enum-key purge of named blob ids is acceptable, but once Phase 2 allows several read keys, any reader could delete blobs another reader still needs. Condition: only a read key scoped to that lane may purge its blobs, and retention stays the backstop.

One-bit refusal and create-only reservations are sound. Conditions: a reservation with no object expires with its URL (300 s), so unused reservations do not hold budget; on lanes whose append token is public (pages' /send/ lanes), blobs only on signed lanes, since anyone holding a public token can otherwise keep the budget reserved and block the owner's writers.

phase_3.opinion: agree with the plan's recommendation, limited to tokens that are not published
phase_3.reason: For a lane whose token is on a public page, signed lanes only (condition above).

Conditions: no request or response bodies in Lambda logs (bodies carry tokens, grants, signer keys and presigned URLs); error responses never echo a token, grant or signature; if S3 server access logs or CloudTrail data events are on for this bucket, they record object keys and presigned query strings, so either leave them off for the append prefix or keep them under the same rule and retention; a test that a write, blob-upload and blob-url leave none of these in the logs.

phase_4.reason: P-256 with raw r||s, domain-separated strings (4.2), strict typed parsing with exact field counts and the 91-byte SPKI (4.3), cheapest checks first (4.4), grant bound to vault and sha256(token), file id from signed content not the signature (malleability), and create-only replay markers (4.1) are sound. Conditions: (1) verification through the cryptography library with the public key loaded from the exact SPKI (rejects points off the curve); reject r or s of 0 or not below the curve order; (2) a signed lane refuses every unsigned write, and refuses a signed write to a lane not in signed mode; (3) the published test vectors include negative cases (wrong domain prefix, DER signature, compressed key, 7-field grant, expired, revoked, replay); (4) state the revocation delay (the config cache TTL) in the docs.

The plan lets a writer use its pki.sgit.ai signing key. That is safe only if nothing else that key signs can produce a string starting 'sg-append/v1|'. sgit pki sign signs files the user chooses; confirm with the pki.sgit.ai developer that its signatures are over a domain-separated message, or use a separate per-lane writer key (preferred, and simple with 4.6's tooling).
Server checks stay P-256 only (4.3). An Ed25519 signature inside the sealed lane.entry is a reader-side matter; settle it in the envelope, not on the server.

A grant can serve as the owner's endorsement of a writer for that lane, so the server enforces it rather than each keeper. But the lane key is a random key, so on its own it says nothing about the owner, and the server is not trusted under the zero-knowledge rule. Conditions: (1) the owner's published key signs the lane key (a domain-separated 'sg-append-lanekey/v1|vault|sha256(token)|sha256(lane SPKI)' statement), and that statement is published with the site's keys; (2) the writer puts grant, signer and signature inside the sealed entry (as the plan suggests) and keepers verify owner key, lane key, grant and signature themselves, not only that the server accepted the write; (3) this covers who may write to the lane; the published key list in site/keys keeps its own owner signatures, because a grant is not public and does not say a key belongs to a person.
Revocation contains a runaway writer within the cache TTL; stats show it. Revisit before outside agents are granted.

Phase 4 must not ship before the 2.9 fail-closed guard, so a rollback can never silently reopen signed lanes. Clients treat a lane as signed only when /limits lists signed-lanes (a.maestro's point 13).

after: I review the Phase 3 and Phase 4 pull requests (code and tests) before each merges to dev, since a merge to dev is a production change.
